title: Reminiscences about Hans Capel
abstract: As an homage to the memory of Hans Willem Capel, I present some personal reminiscences and thoughts that come to my mind in this special occasion.
summary: This paper explores the limitations of classical Boltzmann-Gibbs statistical mechanics when analyzing physical systems exactly at a critical point. It proposes using nonadditive entropic functionals, specifically Tsallis entropy ($S_q$), to develop a more robust theoretical framework. The key finding is that these generalized entropies correctly predict finite physical quantities at $T_c$, unlike standard theory.
main_problem: The paper addresses the failure of traditional Boltzmann-Gibbs (BG) statistics to accurately describe physical systems precisely at a critical point ($T_c$). It seeks an alternative framework using nonadditive entropic functionals.
main_result: Nonadditive entropies, characterized by an index $q$, provide a more physically consistent description of critical phenomena than BG theory, particularly by yielding finite values for generalized critical parameters ($\Gamma_q$) at $T_c$ where BG theory predicts only divergence.
method: The analysis involves comparing theoretical predictions derived from standard BG statistics against those obtained using Tsallis' nonadditive entropy ($S_q$). This comparison is applied to analyze phase transitions and critical exponents in various models.
model_or_system: The study considers general many-body Hamiltonians exhibiting phase transitions, exemplified by ferromagnetic models like the XY or Heisenberg model. The focus is on the behavior of these systems near their critical temperature ($T_c$).
key_observables:
Critical exponents ($\alpha,  eta, \gamma, 
u$), the order parameter ($\eta$), and generalized critical parameters ($\Gamma_q$) are key observables.
important_parameters:
The entropic index $q$ is crucial, as its value determines whether the system's behavior at $T_c$ is described by BG theory ($q=1$) or a nonadditive generalization ($q 
eq 1$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that standard statistical mechanics breaks down exactly at $T_c$, necessitating the use of generalized entropic functionals to capture the true physics.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates how the generalized Gruneisen parameter ($\Gamma_q$) behaves: it diverges for $q>q^*$, vanishes for $q<q^*$, and is finite at a special index $q=q^*$, contrasting sharply with the BG prediction ($q=1$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the limitations of BG theory at criticality, then introducing nonadditive entropies as a mathematical tool to resolve these issues. It develops specific relationships between critical exponents and the entropic index $q$ before presenting quantitative comparisons using generalized parameters.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant because it extends statistical mechanics beyond standard assumptions, providing tools ($S_q$) that can model complex non-equilibrium or strongly interacting regimes where simple thermodynamic limits fail. The connection to dynamical properties (Lyapunov exponents) suggests deep links between entropy formalism and chaos theory.
